title: Conservative Wavefront Traffic Scheduler and Rollback Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a conservative, configurable traffic scheduler ("wavefront" pattern) for model rollouts that prioritizes safety for latency-sensitive customers. The scheduler will support phased exposure, shadowing, deterministic probabilistic splits, time-based and metric-based step schedules, and configurable auto-rollback guardrails. Goal: provide a policy surface that product and platform teams can author in YAML and apply to routes with predictable behavior and observability.
design_notes: Wavefront pattern: begin with small cohort (0.5-2%) and expand in overlapping waves to reduce blast radius while exercising heterogeneity across client segments.
Two scheduling primitives: time-based steps and metric-gated advancement. Admins can compose them (e.g., min-time 30m + p95 < 120ms).
Traffic splitting: deterministic probabilistic split using route key + rollout id as seed to ensure consistent routing for a user across requests (helps session affinity).
Shadow traffic: optional fork mode sending a configurable fraction to new variant without affecting responses, used to gather full-token metrics and regression signals at scale.

Guardrails: continuous evaluation of stability signals (p95 latency, 99th token generation error rate, model-quality regression score from eval harness) with configurable thresholds and decay windows.

Auto-rollback: circuit that triggers a rollback when a threshold breaches for a sustained window; supports automatic rollback or safe-PAUSE where traffic is held and an on-call notification is raised.
Trade-offs considered: conservative exposures increase time-to-full-rollout but dramatically reduce customer-facing regressions. We prioritized predictable safety over rollout speed for P1 customers.
Instrumentation: expose per-step metrics and annotate traces with rollout_id, step_id, cohort_seed for debugging and postmortems.
Policy language: small YAML DSL (see spec) allowing nested conditions, e.g., 'advance_when: any(p95_latency < 120ms, no_regression_for 48h)'.
acceptance_criteria: Policy can be created via YAML and applied to an existing route in the Console and via API.
Scheduler honors deterministic split semantics (same user routed consistently during rollout windows).
Shadow mode can be enabled per-policy; observability pipeline captures token-level metrics for shadowed requests.
Auto-rollback triggers reproducibly when configured thresholds are breached and creates a clear audit trail with rollback reason.
E2E integration tests validate step advancement, metric gating, shadowing, and rollback behavior against a fake model harness.
Performance: additional median latency impact < 2ms for policy evaluation in the hot path when enabled.
Docs: Console UI docs and a playbook published in Confluence and linked from the policy editor.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Spike and prototype scheduler algorithm (ENG spike notes in repo).
Week 2-3: Implement policy evaluator, YAML parser, and deterministic split library (feature branch).
Week 4: Integrate shadowing path into routing; wire metrics collection for shadow requests.
Week 5: Integrate guardrail engine, implement rollback circuit with audit events and notification hooks.
Week 6: Console integration, policy editor additions, and e2e tests.
rollout_playbook: Step 0: Create policy in staging and run shadow at 10% for 24h to gather baseline metrics.
Step 1: Start wavefront rollout: 1% -> 3% -> 8% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with min dwell times of 30m between waves.
Step 2: Each advance requires p95_latency within configured budget AND no model-quality regression exceeding configured delta for the last 60m window.
Automatic rollback: p95 or token-error breaches sustained > 3 consecutive windows triggers automated rollback to previous stable step and notifies on-call via PagerDuty channel 'infra-rollouts'.
Manual intervention path: policy can be paused by the console with immediate hold on further advances; a human can then inspect the shadow logs snapshot and resume or rollback.
Post-rollback: generate 'rollback-reason' artifact and link PR/commit that triggered the rollout; schedule a 2-hour postmortem if impact > medium.
qa_plan: Unit tests for YAML parser and policy evaluator (coverage target 90%).
Integration test harness simulating traffic with variable latency and injected errors to exercise guardrails.
Staging canary: apply policy to internal-staging route and run for 72h with telemetry collected to Grafana dashboard.
Chaos tests: simulate routing agent restart and ensure policy rehydration and idempotence.
Manual QA: run shared prompts suite against shadowed model and verify no silent regressions in semantic QA checks.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Misconfigured thresholds can cause premature rollbacks. Mitigation: provide sane defaults tuned from historical rollouts and require explicit override for P0 customers.
Risk: Deterministic split could reduce randomness for A/B. Mitigation: expose option to use session-affinity vs pure probability depending on product needs.
Risk: Shadow traffic doubles inference cost when enabled. Mitigation: allow sampling and scheduled shadow windows and surface cost estimates in Console before enabling.
Risk: Policy evaluation latency adds to request path. Mitigation: cache policy decisions per route/cohort for short windows and keep evaluator lightweight.
